questions.question: How do flowering plants typically reproduce?
options: By splitting in half through binary fission
Sexually, producing seeds
Solely by producing asexual spores
By growing runners without any flowers

questions.question: Why is plant reproduction so vital for life on Earth?
options: Plants are primary producers that provide food for all animals.
Plants absorb nitrogen directly from the air to feed animals.
Plants generate the soil needed for animal movement.
Plant reproduction is the only source of water in ecosystems.

questions.question: What do flowers contain that make them essential for plant reproduction?
options: Only protective leaves and stems
Both male and female sex organs and gametes
Female gametes only
Male gametes only

questions.question: What is another name for the female gametes in flowering plants?
options: Pollen grains
Ova (egg cells)
Anthers
Stigmas

questions.question: Which plant structures carry the male gametes of a flower?
options: Seeds
Ovules
Pollen grains
Petals

questions.question: What are the three main parts of a seed, and where is the seed formed?
options: Stigma, style, and ovary; formed in the anther
Embryo, pollen grain, and nectar; formed in the stem
Embryo, food store, and a tough outer coat; formed in the ovary
Root, stem, and leaf; formed in the petal

questions.question: What is a fruit in botanical terms?
options: The swollen stem of any photosynthetic plant
A mature, ripened ovary of a seed-producing plant
An unfertilised flower bud that has withered
A protective layer produced by the roots

questions.question: What are the three main natural agents that seeds are adapted to be dispersed by?
options: Sunlight, soil, and rocks
Animals, wind, and water
Heat, cold, and pressure
Insects, worms, and birds only

questions.question: How do pollinators assist in the sexual reproduction of flowering plants?
options: They digest the seeds to help them germinate.
They transfer pollen from one flower to another.
They protect the plant roots from pests.
They provide carbon dioxide directly to the petals.

questions.question: Which group of animals makes up the majority of pollinators, with bees being the largest group?
options: Mammals
Birds
Insects
Reptiles

questions.question: What is meant by the term "food security" in a country or area?
options: Having enough affordable and nutritious food available
Locking up agricultural fields to prevent theft
Relying entirely on imported food supplies
Using artificial chemicals on all crops to preserve them

questions.question: Which statement correctly defines pollination?
options: The fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote
The movement of seeds away from the parent plant
The transfer of pollen from the male anther to the female stigma
The growth of a pollen tube down into the ovary

questions.question: What is a key benefit of cross-pollination compared to self-pollination?
options: It requires no wind or insects to transfer pollen.
It increases genetic variation within a species.
It guarantees that offspring are identical to the parent.
It takes less energy for the plant to produce flowers.

questions.question: In plant reproduction, what is fertilisation?
options: The transfer of pollen grains by wind or insects
The fusion of the nuclei from the male and female gametes
The absorption of minerals from the soil by roots
The shedding of seeds from a ripe fruit

questions.question: What does a fertilised egg cell (zygote) grow into first before becoming a new plant?
options: An embryo
A pollen grain
A mature fruit
An anther

questions.question: When displaying experimental data, when should you use a bar chart instead of a line graph?
options: When the independent variable is continuous
When the independent variable is categoric
When there are no control variables in the investigation
When the dependent variable has very large values

questions.question: Which of these is a common type of seed used in school labs that can easily germinate on wet cotton wool?
options: Oak seeds
Cress seeds
Coconut seeds
Apple seeds

questions.question: In an investigation into the factors affecting seed germination, what is the dependent variable?
options: The variable you change, such as temperature
The variable you measure, such as the number of germinated seeds
The variables you keep the same, like the type of seed
The type of container used to hold the seeds

questions.question: Why must control variables be kept the same during a seed germination investigation?
options: To make sure the independent variable is continuous
To ensure a valid conclusion can be drawn
To guarantee that all seeds germinate at the exact same second
To change the dependent variable more quickly

questions.question: How are wind-dispersed seeds adapted to ensure they can travel far from the parent plant?
options: They are heavy with a thick, sticky outer coat.
They are light with a large surface area.
They are brightly coloured to attract animals.
They are enclosed in juicy, sweet fruits.
